Job Summary

  • The Product Owner is the responsible person to ensure that the bank continues to deliver superior service to our clients by building new capabilities and maintaining existing ones along with all other squad members. The Product Owner works with Clients, business users and stakeholders, risk & compliance colleagues, and Domain colleagues to define in detail what’s needed in order to meet the vision. Thereafter, the Product Owner works closely with the squads to deliver the prioritised vision.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

  • Maximize the business value of the product or service by ensuring we “deliver the right thing at the right time”
  • Responsible for the execution of build and maintain activities for their product or services throughout the lifecycle.
  • Ensure alignment with strategic outcomes and scorecard priorities.
  • Ensure the delivery of the "right thing at the right time," contributing to the Business plan and scorecard outcomes.
  • Craft the vision and concept development of a product.
  • Develop and maintain the roadmap and Squad backlog by liaising with, teams, and key stakeholders or SME's i.e., country / region / product or client and technical specialists.
  • Build strong acceptance criteria for new deliveries that take into account business processes and variations, data quality, system speed and UX.
  • Ensure data-driven prioritization in alignment with strategic outcomes and scorecard.
  • Work with technical counterparts to mitigate technical debt and balance risk, and regulatory items with new features, functionality, or changes to keep the cost of change low.
  • Work in partnership with technology to ensure a balance of functional and non-functional requirements are represented in the backlog and that there is an approach to mitigate or avoid technical debt.
  • Ensures the Product Strategy and Roadmap is transparent, visible, understood by the Delivery Squads and is regularly reviewed with the delivery Squad.
  • Asist to Develop and maintain the roadmap and backlog of the Squad with PO (Products/Services) and Engineering Lead using relevant data points to determine the appropriate roadmap milestones. Regularly review and refine it based on relevant data.
  • Collaborate on technology roadmap and solution with the Engineering Lead, to drive optimum outcomes.
  • Assist to regularly review the Squad performance metrics (both in sprint delivery and the performance after go-live) on a regular basis and to use these insights to execute continuous improvement with the Squad.
  • Build a cadence of measuring business outcomes and benefits. Work closely with markets/segments to ensure that the features can provide the intended benefits which are measured and reviewed in key forums.

Business

  • Engage with clients, stakeholders, and end users and represent their voice on the product backlog.
  • Work closely with Stakeholders to ensure the Product Backlog is created and maintained according to business value/ROI.
  • Facilitate prioritization discussions with all relevant stakeholders including local, regional, country representatives.
  • Optimize value delivery through Continuous Improvement through relevant data and frequent feedback from stakeholders, SMEs, and customers.
  • Engage in continuous backlog management, by refining user stories with clear narratives and acceptance criteria.
  • Prioritize and refine backlog items using data points through collaboration with the technical delivery SMEs.
  • Use lifecycle tools like ADO and Confluence, to plan, track, and manage backlog items.
  • Ensure the Product Backlog is transparent, visible, and understood.
  • Potentially support multiple teams if their backlog items come from the same Product Backlog.

Processes

  • Accountable to ensure the backlog is maintained regularly and backlog user stories are clearly articulated through engagement in continuous backlog management, writing user stories., conducting user story walk-throughs with the delivery Squad and writing clear narratives and acceptance criteria.
  • Accountable to sign off on the delivery of the backlog items (user stories) and ensure the acceptance criteria has been met i.e., through Squad showcases and / or functional walkthroughs of the product / service in use (live).
  • Accountable to ensure backlog is regularly refined, prioritised and worked on with the Squad members.
  • Accountable to ensure sign off of all user stories.
  • Accountable to be present at Squad showcases / demonstrations to support user story sign off and releases.
  • Must be present at team meetings including but not limited to backlog refinement, sprint planning, daily stand up, showcase, retrospectives.
  • Adopt and embed the Change Delivery Standards throughout the lifecycle of the product/service.
  • Adhere to and execute the relevant delivery processes outlined in the Group Enterprise Software Delivery Lifecycle guidelines (eSDLC)
  • Continuously review and consider ways to reduce / eliminate manual processes.
  • Awareness and understanding of the regulatory framework in which the Group operates, and the regulatory requirements and expectations relevant to the role.
  • Participate in the quarterly planning for the Hive and provide steer along with Hive Tech Lead.

People & Talent

  • Collaborate and ensure availability for all meetings as an active, daily as a core member of the squad.
  • Champion and act as a role model of the Group's values and culture.
  • Collaborate daily as a core member of the team.
  • Cultivate a high-performance culture and true ‘self-organising’ team by empowering the Squad, celebrating wins, learning from reviews, and conducting regular retrospectives for continuous improvement.
  • Set direction and drive high performance by translating strategy into clear direction, aligning individual goals to team outcomes and providing regular, constructive feedback.
  • Develop talent and capability through coaching and career conversations that build critical skills, stretch potential and prepare individuals for future opportunities.
  • Lead by example by role-modelling the Bank’s valued behaviours, upholding strong risk and conduct standards, exercising sound judgment, and creating an inclusive team culture that supports wellbeing, values diverse perspectives, and drives accountability.

Risk Management

  • Responsible for effective risk management across all initiatives planed for product.
  • Balance technical debt, risk, and regulatory items with new features, functionality, or changes to keep the cost of change low.

Governance

  • Follow the specified governance process for agile delivery
  • Manage releases and reporting in line with ESDLC standards and other bank governance activities/standards.

Skills And Experience

  • Finantix
  • Wealth Management processes
  • Wealth Product lifecycle
  • Process analysis and Requirements design
  • Communication & Stakeholder management
  • Portfolio Performance Methodology and computation approach
  • Agile Delivery
  • MS office applications – Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Word etc.

Motivations

  • Motivated by delivering high-quality operational outcomes while ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements and internal policies.
  • Energised by identifying opportunities for process improvement, driving operational efficiency, and enhancing customer and stakeholder experiences.
  • Thrives in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment that requires problem-solving, critical thinking, and effective decision-making.
  • Driven by collaborating with cross-functional teams to achieve shared business objectives and deliver sustainable business outcomes.
  • Demonstrates resilience and adaptability when managing complex operational challenges, changing priorities, and continuous business transformation.
  • Motivated by developing people, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement, and supporting team success through coaching and leadership.

Qualifications

  • Agile Product Owner
  • Bachelors / master’s from reputed institutions or equivalent
  • English; Additional Asian languages are a plus

  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

ln:4476985968.descriptionHtml:
The Credit Officer 2 is a seasoned professional role. Applies in-depth disciplinary knowledge, contributing to the development of new techniques and the improvement of processes and work-flow for the area or function. Integrates subject matter and industry expertise within a defined area. Requires in-depth understanding of how areas collectively integrate within the sub-function as well as coordinate and contribute to the objectives of the function and overall business. Evaluates moderately complex and variable issues with substantial potential impact, where development of an approach/taking of an action involves weighing various alternatives and balancing potentially conflicting situations using multiple sources of information. Requires good analytical skills in order to filter, prioritize and validate potentially complex and dynamic material from multiple sources. Strong communication and diplomacy skills are required. Regularly assumes informal/formal leadership role within teams. Involved in coaching and training of new recruits Significant impact in terms of project size, geography, etc. by influencing decisions through advice, counsel and/or facilitating services to others in area of specialization. Work and performance of all teams in the area are directly affected by the performance of the individual.

Responsibilities

  • Develop recommendations to adjust credit policies by analyzing credit and financial performance utilizing statistical scoring, segmentation, regression and simulation techniques
  • Implement initiatives to ensure consistency and compliance with credit policies
  • Utilize SAS in a UNIX environment to perform risk, financial and data analysis including profiling, sampling, reconciliation, and quality testing
  • Prepare risk management presentations for senior management that include analytics on portfolio performance, emerging trends and areas of opportunity
  • Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.


Recommended Qualifications

  • 5-8 years relevant experience
  • Degree in Quantitative Fields such as Economics, Engineering, Operations Research, Business Finance, or Mathematics (Master’s degree preferred)
  • Previous experience in credit card risk management or equivalent training and experience preferably in the financial services industry
  • Ability to apply credit and risk principles toward business goals
  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize, prioritize and drive results with a high sense of urgency
  • Must be highly organized and able to work in a fast paced environment managing multiple projects and possess effective interpersonal, organizational and analytic skills
  • Extensive knowledge of SAS or SQL programming and literacy with MS Office software required


Education

  • Bachelor’s/University degree or equivalent experience


Job Family Group

Risk Management

Job Family

Credit Risk

Time Type

Full time

Most Relevant Skills

Analytical Thinking, Credible Challenge, Financial Analysis, Governance, Policy, Procedure, and Regulation, Risk Management Lifecycle.

Other Relevant Skills

For complementary skills, please see above and/or contact the recruiter.

Citi is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified candidates will receive consideration without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you are a person with a disability and need a reasonable accommodation to use our search tools and/or apply for a career opportunity review Accessibility at Citi.

View Citi’s EEO Policy Statement and the Know Your Rights poster.

ln:4477106178.descriptionHtml:
Citi Commercial Bank offers its clients the convenience, a global banking network, thought leadership and global financial capabilities of Citi. We deliver extensive industry knowledge, local expertise and dedicated service support to Mid-Market companies, with an international footprint. We are focused on providing banking and financial solutions to our clients across 5 key growth industries - Business & Professional Services, Industrials, Digital, Technology & Communications, Consumer and Healthcare.

The primary responsibility of the Associate will be, in cooperation with the Senior Relationship Managers, servicing the banking & financing needs of international Mid-Market clients, deepening existing client relationships and acquiring & onboarding new commercial banking clients.

Responsibilities

  • Build relationships with Citi network and operational teams, becoming one of the key contacts for clients’ requests, internal requests/escalation and resolution.
  • Support Senior Relationship manager in management of assigned portfolio of clients.
  • Work closely with Senior Relationship Managers to ensure we provide a 'Client First' approach and help to deliver outstanding day to day banking & operational support to our Mid-Market clients.
  • In cooperation with Senior Relationship Manager calls on clients and maximise ‘One Citi’ client experience, by proactively leveraging and sharing Citi’s market leading insights, global network and solutions.
  • Monitor and support products’ implementation processes, clients on-boarding process and manage sales CRM platform.
  • Liaise with Relationship Associate to ensure adherence to global KYC (Know Your Customer) standards during the onboarding process and, on an ongoing basis, ensuring the appropriate compliance deliverables are met.
  • Develops and maintains strong ties with Commercial Banking teams across the globe, in particular CCB colleagues working across the same sector vertical, CCB colleagues supporting subsidiary businesses overseas (Commercial Subsidiaries Group). Collaborate and work closely with various product teams (cash sales, trade finance, markets, corporate finance), Underwriting / Risk teams.
  • Work with Senior Relationship Managers to analyse client relationships, risks & opportunities, assists with credit application write-up, financial spreading, deal structuring, returns calculation, documentation review & preparation. Administrate the credit relationship of clients, ensuring the proper application of policies and institutional processes.
  • Understand key commercial banking processes & solutions, including Transactional Banking, FX, Trade, Treasury, Working Capital and Lending products.
  • Support Senior Relationship Managers on solutioning assessment, preparation of pitch books and meeting materials, assists with new clients’ acquisition.
  • Work collaboratively with key internal stakeholders across CCB, share best practice across teams in order to deliver 'best in class' relationship management to new and existing clients.
  • Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behaviour, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.


Qualifications

  • 5-8 years of experience
  • Previous banking experience
  • Working within Commercial/Corporate banking is desirable.
  • Experience in a Client Relationship role or client facing role.
  • Sales, presentation and communication skills. Focus on first class service quality.

ln:4475750258.descriptionHtml:
Job Summary

  • Work in PCVC team to manage the Product control activities for China across Business
  • Provide strong oversight of the integrity, accuracy and timely reporting of China trading revenues, balance sheet positions and valuation adjustments, ensuring that financial results are appropriately controlled and understood.
  • Support Team Head to establish and maintain a China-specific Product Control and Valuation Control framework that meets local regulatory requirements while remaining aligned with the bank’s global policies, standards and risk appetite.
  • Partner with Front Office, Risk, Finance and Operations to support sustainable business growth by providing independent challenge, identifying emerging financial and valuation risks, and enabling informed commercial decision-making.
  • Strengthen the local control environment through effective governance, clear ownership, high-quality management information and the development of capable China-based Product Control and Valuation Control resources.
  • Manage the Valuation Control deliverables as applicable for China regulatory requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Key contributor to China-based Product Control and Valuation Control team, acting as a hands-on subject matter expert. The role combines teamwork and significant individual contribution, particularly in resolving complex control, valuation, accounting and regulatory matters.
  • Oversee the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of daily and monthly P&L, balance sheet substantiation, valuation adjustments, independent price verification and other core Product Control and Valuation Control activities for the China business.
  • Support team leader to establish and maintain an effective China-specific control framework that meets local regulatory expectations and is aligned with the bank’s global Product Control and Valuation Control policies, methodologies and governance standards.
  • Coordinate extensively with global and regional Product Control and Valuation Control teams to obtain technical input, clarify policy requirements, resolve methodology differences and ensure consistent application of global standards within the China business.
  • Provide independent review and challenge of trading results, valuation methodologies, reserves, model inputs, adjustments and balance sheet positions. Ensure material issues are identified, investigated, escalated and resolved within agreed timelines.
  • Partner with Front Office, Risk, Finance, Operations, Treasury, Compliance and Technology to support new products, business growth and regulatory initiatives, ensuring that appropriate financial controls and valuation processes are in place before implementation.
  • Support the China business by providing clear analysis of revenue performance, valuation uncertainty, balance sheet risks, control weaknesses and emerging issues, enabling informed management and commercial decision-making.
  • Manage regulatory and internal stakeholder requirements, including preparation of management information, responses to regulatory enquiries, audit support, remediation plans and evidence of sustainable control improvements.
  • Key contributor to achieve improvements in processes, reporting, data quality and automation, reducing manual adjustments and recurring breaks while improving the transparency, efficiency and resilience of the control environment.
  • Maintain effective governance over material issues, exceptions and control breaches, with clear ownership, action plans, escalation thresholds and reporting to relevant China, regional and global committees.
  • The role holder is responsible for both the day-to-day effectiveness of the local Product Control and Valuation Control function and the successful coordination of China requirements with the wider global control organisation.

Skills And Experience

  • Product Control and Valuation Control understanding
  • Financial Markets and Trading Products
  • China Regulatory awareness
  • Control Framework and risk management
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Analytical and Communication skills
  • Valuation knowledge – IPV/FVA/PVA

Motivations

  • Operating in a complex and evolving China regulatory environment, where local requirements may differ from global standards and require careful interpretation, escalation and practical implementation.
  • Resolving valuation, P&L and balance sheet issues involving incomplete data, methodology differences, manual processes or unclear ownership across local, regional and global teams.
  • Building a credible and sustainable local Product Control and Valuation Control framework while working with limited resources, competing priorities and significant dependency on global subject-matter experts.
  • Managing periods of heightened regulatory, audit or senior-management scrutiny, requiring timely responses, clear evidence of control effectiveness and disciplined delivery of remediation commitments.
  • Challenging senior business and functional stakeholders on valuation assumptions, manual adjustments, control weaknesses and financial risks, while maintaining constructive relationships and supporting business objectives.
  • Driving long-term process and control improvements where solutions require coordination across multiple teams, changes to systems or data, and sustained follow-through rather than short-term fixes.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across different regulatory, cultural and organisational environments, adapting o global frameworks and local requirements while preserving appropriate governance, control and consistency
  • Proven Experience dealing complex issues through ambiguity, bringing together multiple stakeholders, forming a clear view from incomplete conflicting information and driving decisions and remediation through to sustainable closure
  • CICPA & CFA is preferred
  • Languages: Chinese and English

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Coverage Banking Graduate Programme 2027

Join our Coverage Banking team and help build and deepen relationships with some of the world’s leading corporates, financial institutions, investors and public sector clients. As the client-facing arm of the Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB) franchise, Coverage Banking sits at the centre of our client relationships, bringing together product expertise, sector insights and market connectivity to deliver holistic banking solutions.

With a unique footprint across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, you’ll gain exposure to global clients, cross-border transactions and strategic conversations that shape industries, economies and communities. From supporting capital raising and financing solutions to helping clients navigate growth, transformation and market opportunities, you’ll play a role in delivering outcomes that matter.

About the Graduate Programme – how you’ll learn and grow

Join a skills-first organisation where your potential matters more than your background. Over our two-year graduate programme, you’ll gain hands-on experience, build lasting relationships and grow your understanding of clients, markets and the wider business. From day one, you’ll contribute to meaningful work and be supported to build a successful long-term career.

You’ll Benefit From

  • Real impact: Take ownership of meaningful work that contributes to business outcomes.
  • Future-ready capabilities: Build the technical, commercial and professional skills needed to succeed.
  • Global collaboration: Work with colleagues and clients across markets, products and functions.
  • Continuous growth: Learn from structured development, mentoring and practical experience

Where you could work

You’ll be placed into one of the following teams, working as an Associate Coverage Banker supporting senior bankers in managing client relationships, coordinating deal execution and identifying opportunities across the Bank’s network.

  • Corporate Coverage: Partner with multinational corporations, large local corporates and mid-market clients across a broad range of industries. You’ll help deliver banking solutions spanning financing, cash management, trade, capital markets and strategic advisory services, while supporting relationship teams in driving client growth and franchise deepening.
  • Financial Institutions Coverage: Support relationships with banks, insurance companies, asset managers, sovereign entities, public sector organisations and other financial institutions. You’ll gain exposure to complex client needs across financing, risk management, transaction banking, securities services and investment solutions.
  • Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A): Support clients through significant moments of transformation, including acquisitions, divestments, mergers and strategic partnerships. You’ll gain exposure to transaction execution, financial analysis, industry research and deal processes while working closely with sector bankers and product specialists.

Bring the skills - we’ll help you build your career

We welcome students from all degree disciplines and backgrounds, recognising that diverse perspectives drive innovation.

We’re Looking For People Who Can

  • Take ownership and demonstrate initiative.
  • Think critically and solve problems in a structured way.
  • Learn quickly and adapt to new challenges, seeking opportunities to grow and develop
  • Build strong relationships and collaborate effectively with others
  • Communicate confidently and collaborate across different cultures and backgrounds.
  • Demonstrate commercial curiosity and an interest in global markets, industries and clients.
  • Thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced and international environment.

For technical roles, we particularly value backgrounds in Finance & Banking, Economics, Accounting, Mathematics and Statistics.

Eligibility

To be eligible for this graduate programme, you need to be in your final year of study and graduating by July 2027. You must also have the permanent legal right to work in the country you’re applying to.

You can only submit one application within a six-month period, so take time to review our opportunities and apply for the role that best fits your interests, skills and career goals.

Key Dates

  • Assessment Centres: October 2026 onwards
  • Start Date: July 2027

About Corporate & Investment Banking (CIB)

We are a super-connector for many of the world’s largest companies across more than 50 markets, playing a central role in global trade, capital flows and economic growth. We work with governments, financial institutions, and some of the world’s most ambitious corporates to help them expand, invest, and navigate uncertainty across increasingly complex and fast-changing markets.

What makes us distinctive is our combination of deep local expertise with an extensive and unique global network. We support clients across risk management, financing, transaction services, advisory, and sustainable finance, helping move capital to where it’s needed most and supporting the real economy across our footprint.

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

Recruitment Assessments

Some of our roles use assessments to help us understand how suitable you are for the role you've applied to. If you are invited to take an assessment, this is great news. It means your application has progressed to an important stage of our recruitment process.

Visit our careers website www.sc.com/careers

What We Offer

Key Responsibilities

  • As a Product Owner in our cross-functional squads, the candidate will drive the outcomes of the squad to deliver on their objectives and key results. You will build and prioritise the product backlog to achieve business goals and manage stakeholder relationships to align expectation, prioritisation and overall product roadmap.

Strategy

  • The primary purpose of this position is to develop and transform Capital Markets Products & Solutions (CMPS) product capability to provide digital channels for both clients and internal users across Private Banking and Retail Banking.
  • The Bank is aiming to grow product capability through digital and self-direct channels. This Product Owner (PO) role is to drive the agile technology projects to establish a robust price discovery and execution platform. It is also required to build system interface with upstream systems (e.g. client information check) and downstream systems (e.g. booking trades into core banking platforms) to streamline operation flow and improve users (including clients) experience and frontline productivity.
  • As PO, you will develop and maintain a vision for agile technology projects and be responsible for communicating the vision to the scrum team. Be responsible for agile technology projects and features from concept to final implementation. In particular,
  • Have a good understanding of wealth management products, it's processes and relevance to clients.
  • Define and own the strategic digital product vision and roadmap for the wealth management product suite.
  • Align product strategy with business goals, market trends, and client needs.
  • Develop a competitive product strategy across relevant asset classes (such as FX, equities, fixed income, structured products, OTC derivatives, funds, and insurance.)
  • Monitor market dynamics and regulatory changes, ensuring products remain competitive and compliant.
  • As PO you will work with architects, business stakeholders and development teams to ensure that business, quality and functional goals are met with each release. Be responsible for the design, usability, quality and delivery of agile technology projects and features.
  • As the subject matter expert, this role is to determine business requirements, review technology project plans from the business perspective, and ensure new technology capabilities are embedded in business processes to deliver benefits. Ensure smooth execution on the ground, and communicate the changes delivered to relevant stakeholders including front office.

Business

  • Review and understand key business policies and processes in Wealth Management in offering CMPS products and services to both private banking and retail banking clients. Identify critical pain-points and articulate how planned / in-flight technology projects will solve them.
  • As Product Owner (PO), specialized in Digital platforms, should be familiar with the development of CMPS order management/ execution platforms and ensure that it is properly interfaced with multiple downstream booking systems.
  • The PO should have strong technical knowhow to improve front office systems performance and expand product penetration according to the business development.

Processes

  • The PO is the key decision maker on priorities and design decisions, and work to ensure that all stakeholders are aligned at each stage of the agile development lifecycle (when a new project is created). The PO also needs to understand both the engineering and business side of releases and be ultimately responsible for representing the end user’s needs.
  • Provide business input on requirements to the technology project teams. Work with subject-matter experts in product teams, front office and operations on requirements (e.g., a new electronic workflow to simplify layers of checking, or to auto-populate repeated fields in client forms). Prioritise “must have” items vs. “good to have”.
  • Review technology plans and design specifications, to ensure business requirements are met and that benefits will be delivered. Identify impact on critical processes within the Bank’s operational risk framework, and work with process owners and project teams to ensure robust controls.
  • Work with technology project teams to develop test plans. Co-ordinate business users to test new platforms or technology features that are developed. Ensure final delivery meets user needs.
  • Work with stakeholders in the front, middle and back offices to ensure successful “go live” of projects, from the business perspective. Develop training material, co-ordinate briefings, design and execute communication plans. Gather feedback post-implementation, and track benefits captured.
  • Participate in project review meetings and identify/highlight any potential issue that may impact project’s cost, timeline and/or scope and work with concerned stakeholders for its early resolution to bring back the project on track.
  • Conduct periodic briefings to senior management on progress of technology projects, from the business perspective. Highlight issues that require resolution.

People & Talent

  • Work towards strengthening the performance culture and reinforcement of accountabilities in products. Sharing the technical skills and experience with other team members.

Risk Management

  • Embed a risk culture that supports the Bank’s strategy and philosophy for the management of risk.
  • Ensure that effective arrangements are in place within WM in the region for the prevention of money laundering in line with the Group Policy and Standards, respective country regulatory guidelines and local legal requirements. In particular, ensure that the obligations on reporting suspicious activities are met.
  • Ensure that Risk Management matters that are brought to the job holder’s attention are subject to direct remedial action and/or ensure adequate reporting to the relevant Risk Committees

Governance

  • At all times have an awareness and understanding of the regulatory framework, in which the Group operates, and the regulatory requirements and expectations relevant to the role.

Regulatory & Business Conduct

  • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
  • Lead the business to achieve the outcomes set out in the Bank’s Conduct Principles
  • Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

Key stakeholders

  • Regional and Country Wealth Management Heads and WM Product Managers.
  • Key markets Segment Heads, IAs and RMs
  • Market/Credit/Operational Risk, Legal, Compliance, Middle Office and COO team

Other Responsibilities

  • Perform other responsibilities assigned by Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures
  • To achieve other business and non-financial objectives
  • To drive the Bank’s strategy and franchise development
  • To ensure that the business is conducted in an operationally robust environment
  • To ensure compliance with regulations and controls as set by the Bank and external regulatory authorities

Skills And Experience

  • Strong risk evaluation experience in Capital Markets / Wealth Management products
  • An ideal candidate should have 5 years of experience in technology & business
  • Extensive knowledge in financial market products

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 5-8 years of experience in wealth management, investment banking, or financial services.
  • Good understanding of wealth management products and asset classes (example FX, equities, fixed income, structured products, OTC derivatives, funds, and insurance.)
  • Relevant knowledge of regulatory and operational frameworks in wealth management.
  • Preferred: Understanding of global wealth management market trends.
  • Relevant degree from reputable university
  • Project Management / System Development or equivalent
  • mandatory & developmental – role specific and regulatory/compliance bank wide specific
  • Proficient English

Key Responsibilities
- As a Product Owner in our cross-functional squads, the candidate will drive the outcomes of the squad to deliver on their objectives and key results. You will build and prioritise the product backlog to achieve business goals and manage stakeholder relationships to align expectation, prioritisation and overall product roadmap.
Strategy
- The primary purpose of this position is to develop and transform Capital Markets Products & Solutions (CMPS) product capability to provide digital channels for both clients and internal users across Private Banking and Retail Banking.
- The Bank is aiming to grow product capability through digital and self-direct channels. This Product Owner (PO) role is to drive the agile technology projects to establish a robust price discovery and execution platform. It is also required to build system interface with upstream systems (e.g. client information check) and downstream systems (e.g. booking trades into core banking platforms) to streamline operation flow and improve users (including clients) experience and frontline productivity.
- As PO, you will develop and maintain a vision for agile technology projects and be responsible for communicating the vision to the scrum team. Be responsible for agile technology projects and features from concept to final implementation. In particular,
- Have a good understanding of wealth management products, it's processes and relevance to clients.
- Define and own the strategic digital product vision and roadmap for the wealth management product suite.
- Align product strategy with business goals, market trends, and client needs.
- Develop a competitive product strategy across relevant asset classes (such as FX, equities, fixed income, structured products, OTC derivatives, funds, and insurance.)
- Monitor market dynamics and regulatory changes, ensuring products remain competitive and compliant.
- As PO you will work with architects, business stakeholders and development teams to ensure that business, quality and functional goals are met with each release. Be responsible for the design, usability, quality and delivery of agile technology projects and features.
- As the subject matter expert, this role is to determine business requirements, review technology project plans from the business perspective, and ensure new technology capabilities are embedded in business processes to deliver benefits. Ensure smooth execution on the ground, and communicate the changes delivered to relevant stakeholders including front office.
Business
- Review and understand key business policies and processes in Wealth Management in offering CMPS products and services to both private banking and retail banking clients. Identify critical pain-points and articulate how planned / in-flight technology projects will solve them.
- As Product Owner (PO), specialized in Digital platforms, should be familiar with the development of CMPS order management/ execution platforms and ensure that it is properly interfaced with multiple downstream booking systems.
- The PO should have strong technical knowhow to improve front office systems performance and expand product penetration according to the business development.
Processes
- The PO is the key decision maker on priorities and design decisions, and work to ensure that all stakeholders are aligned at each stage of the agile development lifecycle (when a new project is created). The PO also needs to understand both the engineering and business side of releases and be ultimately responsible for representing the end user’s needs.
- Provide business input on requirements to the technology project teams. Work with subject-matter experts in product teams, front office and operations on requirements (e.g., a new electronic workflow to simplify layers of checking, or to auto-populate repeated fields in client forms). Prioritise “must have” items vs. “good to have”.
- Review technology plans and design specifications, to ensure business requirements are met and that benefits will be delivered. Identify impact on critical processes within the Bank’s operational risk framework, and work with process owners and project teams to ensure robust controls.
- Work with technology project teams to develop test plans. Co-ordinate business users to test new platforms or technology features that are developed. Ensure final delivery meets user needs.
- Work with stakeholders in the front, middle and back offices to ensure successful “go live” of projects, from the business perspective. Develop training material, co-ordinate briefings, design and execute communication plans. Gather feedback post-implementation, and track benefits captured.
- Participate in project review meetings and identify/highlight any potential issue that may impact project’s cost, timeline and/or scope and work with concerned stakeholders for its early resolution to bring back the project on track.
- Conduct periodic briefings to senior management on progress of technology projects, from the business perspective. Highlight issues that require resolution.
- Work towards strengthening the performance culture and reinforcement of accountabilities in products. Sharing the technical skills and experience with other team members.
Risk Management
- Embed a risk culture that supports the Bank’s strategy and philosophy for the management of risk.
- Ensure that effective arrangements are in place within WM in the region for the prevention of money laundering in line with the Group Policy and Standards, respective country regulatory guidelines and local legal requirements. In particular, ensure that the obligations on reporting suspicious activities are met.
- Ensure that Risk Management matters that are brought to the job holder’s attention are subject to direct remedial action and/or ensure adequate reporting to the relevant Risk Committees
Governance
- At all times have an awareness and understanding of the regulatory framework, in which the Group operates, and the regulatory requirements and expectations relevant to the role.
- Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
- Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
- Lead the business to achieve the outcomes set out in the Bank’s Conduct Principles
- Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.
Key stakeholders
- Regional and Country Wealth Management Heads and WM Product Managers.
- Key markets Segment Heads, IAs and RMs
- Market/Credit/Operational Risk, Legal, Compliance, Middle Office and COO team
Other Responsibilities
- Perform other responsibilities assigned by Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures
- To achieve other business and non-financial objectives
- To drive the Bank’s strategy and franchise development
- To ensure that the business is conducted in an operationally robust environment
- To ensure compliance with regulations and controls as set by the Bank and external regulatory authorities
Skills And Experience
- Strong risk evaluation experience in Capital Markets / Wealth Management products
- An ideal candidate should have 5 years of experience in technology & business
- Extensive knowledge in financial market products
Qualifications

- Good understanding of wealth management products and asset classes (example FX, equities, fixed income, structured products, OTC derivatives, funds, and insurance.)
- Relevant knowledge of regulatory and operational frameworks in wealth management.
- Preferred: Understanding of global wealth management market trends.
- Relevant degree from reputable university
- Project Management / System Development or equivalent
- mandatory & developmental – role specific and regulatory/compliance bank wide specific
- Proficient English

The Research Associate is a developing professional role. Deals with most problems independently and has some latitude to solve complex problems. Integrates in-depth specialty area knowledge with a solid understanding of industry standards and practices. Good understanding of how the team and area integrate with others in accomplishing the objectives of the sub function/ job family. Applies analytical thinking and knowledge of data analysis tools and methodologies. Requires attention to detail when making judgments and recommendations based on the analysis of factual information. Typically deals with variable issues with potentially broader business impact. Applies professional judgment when interpreting data and results. Breaks down information in a systematic and communicable manner. Developed communication and diplomacy skills are required in order to exchange potentially complex/sensitive information. Moderate but direct impact through close contact with the businesses' core activities. Quality and timeliness of service provided will affect the effectiveness of own team and other closely related teams.

Responsibilities

  • Reviews and processes broker votes to be shared and consumed
  • Organizes the product management team including creation of presentations, marketing schedules, coordination of the marketing diary, product planning meetings, diary management etc.
  • Publishes focus list notes, updating and displaying the new focus list posters etc.
  • Contributes to market data and subscriptions management for Equity Research
  • Responsible for collation, co-ordination and organization of Road Ahead conference, stock steering meetings
  • Assists with year-end scorecard preparation, result analysis, goals and training
  • Provides management information including variance analysis, month-end reporting etc.
  • Conducts expense management including travel and entertainment pre-approvals, client interaction spend pre-approval e.g. GLG, non-network individuals etc.
  • Manages and prepares Committee quality reviews
  • Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, demonstrating particular consideration for the firm's reputation and safeguarding Citigroup, its clients and assets, by driving compliance with applicable laws, rules and regulations, adhering to Policy, applying sound ethical judgment regarding personal behavior, conduct and business practices, and escalating, managing and reporting control issues with transparency.


Qualifications

  • Existing knowledge of Research or external Investment research division essential
  • History of working within tight deadlines and prioritization
  • Microsoft systems especially Excel and Word

  • Accuracy and attention to detail
  • Secure and maintain applicable licenses


Education

Research

Research Analysis

Full time

ln:4470484888.descriptionHtml:
Ready to shape Corporate Sales growth for Strategic and Focus clients?

Why HSBC

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world. Guided by our purpose of opening up a world of opportunity, our ambition is to become the world’s most trusted bank globally, putting customers at the heart of everything we do.

The Role

Corporate Sales sits within HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB) and supports corporate clients with relevant products, solutions and market insight. This role focuses on serving Strategic and Focus clients, building trusted relationships and improving product penetration and wallet share. You’ll manage revenue and profitability across an allocated client portfolio while delivering a high standard of service from idea through to execution and post-trade. The role also has a strong focus on improving the cost of service delivery including shifting transactional activity towards e-capability where appropriate. Where supervisory responsibilities apply, you’ll set direction for the local Corporate Sales team and maintain a strong control environment across front office activity. Success means measurable portfolio growth, strong client feedback and consistent delivery in line with HSBC policies and regulatory expectations.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Manage a portfolio of Strategic and Focus corporate clients with clear ownership of revenue performance
  • Identify sales opportunities end-to-end from client need through execution and post-trade support
  • Provide day-to-day coverage across the Corporate Sales offering, coordinating with trading teams to support execution flow
  • Develop client relationships that strengthen product penetration and expand share of wallet across priority accounts
  • Partner with Relationship Managers, Global Payments Solutions (GPS) and Global Trade Solutions (GTS) to meet client needs
  • Champion adoption of appropriate service models such as migrating transactional activity to self-service e-capability
  • Coordinate with Corporate Risk Solutions (CRS) for complex balance sheet structuring solutions and cross-sell opportunities
  • Maintain an effective control environment, escalating unusual or unacceptable activity and supporting fair customer outcomes
  • Oversee team activity where supervisory responsibilities apply including performance management, coaching and resource planning
  • Adapt processes as technology platforms evolve while keeping service quality and risk controls front of mind

What We're Looking For

  • Bring strong experience in Corporate Sales including knowledge of products, clients, systems and key processes
  • Apply established understanding of capital markets including foreign exchange instruments and interest rate derivatives
  • Manage transaction flow from order through to execution in partnership with trading teams and internal stakeholders
  • Demonstrate a track record of developing client relationships that translate into revenue growth and deeper product usage
  • Partner effectively across teams and regions to deliver coordinated client coverage and consistent service
  • Operate within regulatory requirements for non-advisory sales and trading activities including holding relevant local or cross-border exams and qualifications or equivalent demonstrable experience
  • Apply sound judgement in managing conduct risk, financial crime risk and operational risk within a front office environment
  • Supervise and develop team members where applicable including performance management, coaching and maintaining quality of output

Building deeper Corporate Sales relationships

This role offers the chance to shape how HSBC supports Strategic and Focus corporate clients across products, execution and service models. You’ll be central to improving client outcomes while strengthening revenue performance and operational efficiency. Where supervisory responsibilities apply, you’ll also create clarity on standards and controls and support a consistent approach to front office supervision.

If you want your work to be measured in client trust, disciplined execution and sustainable growth this role is a strong platform to build from. Apply to help expand the HSBC Corporate Sales franchise through relationships that last and solutions that land well in market.

ln:4475942655.descriptionHtml:
Some Careers Have More Impact Than Others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Consultant Specialist .

Business: Hong Kong Technology

Principal Responsibilities

Work as Agile Lead on building DSP 3.0 as a Key Responsiblities.

  • Lead delivery of DSP 3.0 outcomes by enabling squads to ship agreed platform capabilities (e.g., core services, integration patterns, controls) predictably and at pace.
  • Establish and run effective agile ways of working (ceremonies, cadence, backlog hygiene, Definition of Ready/Done) so the programme delivers consistent value each sprint/PI.
  • Own end-to-end delivery governance and transparency across squads, providing clear plans, dependencies, risks/issues, delivery metrics, and stakeholder updates.
  • Drive cross-team alignment and dependency management with Architecture, Engineering, Data, Security, Risk/Controls, and Operations to ensure coordinated delivery.
  • Remove impediments and unblock execution by actively resolving blockers, escalating early, and ensuring timely decisions from the right forums.
  • Enable strong product ownership and prioritisation by partnering with Product Owners to shape outcomes, manage scope, and maintain a value-driven roadmap.
  • Embed quality, resilience, and controls-by-design into delivery (testing strategy, non-functional requirements, release readiness, operational support model).
  • Support sustainable change and adoption by coordinating release planning, communications, training needs, and feedback loops with consumer teams.
  • Build a high-performing, inclusive team culture that promotes continuous improvement, psychological safety, and shared accountability for outcomes.

Requirements

Skill set to succeed as an Agile Lead for building DSP 3.0

Agile delivery leadership (core)

  • Strong facilitation of agile ceremonies (planning, refinement, review, retro) with outcomes, not theatre.
  • Coaching squads on pragmatic agile practices (flow, WIP limits, DoR/DoD, estimation that fits the team).

Programme execution & governance

  • Planning across multiple squads (roadmaps, sprint/PI planning, milestones, release trains).
  • Dependency mapping and active management (tech, data, security, environments, vendors).

Platform/product thinking (DSP 3.0 context)

  • Understanding platform operating models: “build once, reuse many”, self-service, developer experience.
  • Ability to shape work into consumable capabilities (APIs, data products, patterns, reusable components).

Technical fluency (enough to be dangerous, not to code)

  • Comfort with engineering concepts: CI/CD, branching/release strategies, environments, automated testing.
  • Familiarity with data/platform basics: data pipelines, APIs, event streaming, metadata/lineage (as relevant).
  • Non-functional requirements: resilience, performance, observability, capacity, and supportability.

Risk, controls, and regulatory awareness (banking essential)

  • Experience embedding controls into delivery (evidence, traceability, approvals, audit-ready artefacts).
  • Working knowledge of security-by-design, change management, and operational readiness expectations.
  • Ability to partner effectively with Risk, Compliance, Security, and Control Owners without slowing delivery.

Stakeholder management & communication

  • Confident senior stakeholder engagement (clear asks, crisp updates, decision logs).
  • Translating between business, data, engineering, and control functions—reducing “lost in translation” tax.

Continuous improvement & metrics

  • Using metrics to improve flow: throughput, cycle time, lead time, defect trends, sprint predictability.
  • Facilitating retros that lead to real change (experiments, owners, measurable outcomes).
  • Strong problem-solving/root-cause analysis (e.g., 5 Whys, fishbone) applied to delivery issues.

Team culture & leadership presence

  • Building psychological safety and inclusive collaboration across diverse teams and geographies.
  • Conflict resolution and healthy challenge (keeping debates about ideas, not people).
  • Coaching individuals (POs, Scrum Masters, Engineers) and growing delivery maturity over time.

You’ll achieve more when you join HSBC.

HSBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and, opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. We encourage applications from all suitably qualified persons irrespective of, but not limited to, their gender or genetic information, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, social status, medical care leave requirements, political affiliation, people with disabilities, color, national origin, veteran status, etc., We consider all applications based on merit and suitability to the role.

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

ln:4475953160.descriptionHtml:
Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB)

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Through our international network, we connect emerging and mature markets, covering key growth areas. We partner with our corporate, government and institutional clients to help them achieve consistent, long-term performance. Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team.

In This Role, You Will

Business：To maximize the revenues of customer portfolio and increase the Bank's share of customer wallets. To maintain a high level of credit quality in the jobholder's customer portfolio and to mitigate the hidden risks of evolving products.

  • Assist Associate Director/ Director to:
  • Co-ordinate origination and execution of in-country activities across the spectrum of banking products/service.
  • Build the Banking franchise value/reputation in the market place.
  • Drive achievement against targets for revenue generation, product alignment, customer satisfaction and cost containment.
  • Combine client relationship management with strong risk assessment and management capabilities ensuring the required credit quality & requisite returns on risk.
  • Identify event driven opportunities on an opportunistic basis, bringing in sector/country expertise as appropriate.
  • Aggressively grow HSBC's share of client wallet involving product specialists to ensure product capabilities are in line with client/sector requirements.
  • By critically assessing the exposures of each customer through vigorous review processes, active communications with CST members and frequent update of market intelligence. Such reviews are to be completed on time as required by the account review cycle and also where deemed necessary.
  • By working closely with Credit Risk Management to ensure that all credits are in compliance of both internal and external requirements and to formulate / implement exit or rehabilitation strategies for substandard credits. The primary goals are to safeguard the Bank for any material loss and to obtain an optimal balance between risk and return.
  • Customers and Stakeholders：To build effective customer relationships and to become the customers' preferred financial partner and trusted advisor.
  • By ensuring customers' experiences with the Bank in all front exceed their expectations, i.e. first class services are provided promptly and professionally; solutions presented are competitive and innovative.
  • By keeping abreast of the customer's business development through frequent contacts in both official and social occasions.
  • By providing advisory-led value added services to customers with the jobholder's updated sector knowledge and market intelligence.
  • To assist senior bankers in ensuring focused relationship building programs are carried out regularly
  • Leadership & Teamwork: To coordinate the Customer Service Team (CST) to ensure the clients' needs are covered in a proactive and efficient manner.
  • By effectively utilizing customer relationship management tool (i.e. CME).
  • By managing client meetings and ensuring that product partners actively participate in discussions concerning client requirements and needs.
  • Operational Effectiveness & Control: To support the senior bankers in operational issues.
  • By working closely with customers to identify macro-operating issues and to satisfy their requirements on a regional /local basis.
  • Understand and ensure compliance with all relevant internal and external rules, regulations and procedures that apply to the conduct of the business in which the jobholder is involved.
  • Maintain HSBC internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators.

To be successful in the role, you should meet the following requirements:

  • Ability to provide marketing support to senior relationship managers
  • Ability to establish rapport with members of client's management team
  • Ability to provide good analytical support to senior relationship managers
  • Strong PC skills (excel, powerpoint etc)
  • Good team player
  • Knowledge of HSBC Group structures and products
  • Good verbal and written communication skills
  • Knowledge of the spectrum of banking products and services
  • Understanding of risk management and credit mitigants
  • Good level of financial analysis ability

You’ll achieve more at HSBC.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within and inclusive and diverse environment. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

- By working closely with Credit Risk Management to ensure that all credits are in compliance of both internal and external requirements and to formulate / implement exit or rehabilitation strategies for substandard credits. The primary goals are to safeguard the Bank for any material loss and to obtain an optimal balance between risk and return.
- Customers and Stakeholders：To build effective customer relationships and to become the customers' preferred financial partner and trusted advisor.
- By ensuring customers' experiences with the Bank in all front exceed their expectations, i.e. first class services are provided promptly and professionally; solutions presented are competitive and innovative.
- By keeping abreast of the customer's business development through frequent contacts in both official and social occasions.
- By providing advisory-led value added services to customers with the jobholder's updated sector knowledge and market intelligence.
- To assist senior bankers in ensuring focused relationship building programs are carried out regularly
- Leadership & Teamwork: To coordinate the Customer Service Team (CST) to ensure the clients' needs are covered in a proactive and efficient manner.
- By effectively utilizing customer relationship management tool (i.e. CME).
- By managing client meetings and ensuring that product partners actively participate in discussions concerning client requirements and needs.
- Operational Effectiveness & Control: To support the senior bankers in operational issues.
- By working closely with customers to identify macro-operating issues and to satisfy their requirements on a regional /local basis.
- Understand and ensure compliance with all relevant internal and external rules, regulations and procedures that apply to the conduct of the business in which the jobholder is involved.
- Maintain HSBC internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit points together with any issues raised by external regulators.
- Ability to provide marketing support to senior relationship managers
- Ability to establish rapport with members of client's management team
- Ability to provide good analytical support to senior relationship managers
- Strong PC skills (excel, powerpoint etc)
- Good team player
- Knowledge of HSBC Group structures and products
- Good verbal and written communication skills
- Knowledge of the spectrum of banking products and services
- Understanding of risk management and credit mitigants
- Good level of financial analysis ability
You’ll achieve more at HSBC.
Issued by HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited

ln:4475950398.descriptionHtml:
Corporate and Institutional Banking (CIB)

HSBC Corporate and Institutional Banking is a markets-led, financing-focused business that provides investment and financial solutions. Through our international network, we connect emerging and mature markets, covering key growth areas. We partner with our corporate, government and institutional clients to help them achieve consistent, long-term performance. Our products and services include advisory, financing, prime services, research and analysis, securities services, trading and sales and transaction banking.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team.

In This Role, You Will

  • Responsible for the delivery of Business Credit Office (BCO) tasks in line with agreed OKRs, SLAs and KPIs
  • Own the end-to-end Credit & Lending servicing journey, ensuring a seamless and efficient process for customers and internal stakeholders
  • Combine client relationship management with strong risk assessment and management capabilities ensuring the required credit quality & requisite returns on risk
  • Continuously drive improvement in their productivity whilst enhancing client experience.
  • Adopt technology and customer experience improvement initiatives, including alignment to a globally consistent C&L operating model and active participation in training initiatives
  • Participate in deal discussions and meetings with clients or credit risk as required
  • Strong execution and implementation ability.
  • Ability to build and maintain strong relationships across the teams, including credibility with both Business and Risk leaders.
  • Protect the Bank by acting as First Line of Defence and adhering to all controls
  • Maintain HSBC internal control standards, including timely implementation of internal and external audit recomentations, along with addressing any issues raised by external regulators
  • Demonstrates ability to engage in constructive and consistent dialogue with risk partners, in a manner that effectively balances commercial outcomes and risk management
  • Work with the BCO Team Lead to ensure adequate credit risk management controls are built into the operational process and robust MI is in place to track and measure risk against agreed thresholds

To be successful in the role, you should meet the following requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or a related field
  • Corporate lending experience with strong analytical skills and sound credit knowledge
  • Strong understanding of various financing instruments and banking products for Wholesale Banking
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to navigate complex situations and drive alignment among senior leaders
  • Clear understanding of the Group credit risk principles, policies and statutory compliances
  • Strong commercial mindset
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all levels of the organization

You’ll achieve more at HSBC.

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within and inclusive and diverse environment. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

Issued by HSBC Bank (China) Company Limited
